answer: Latency triangulation. Each epoch three verifiers in beacon-picked regions ping every key 20 times at random moments, and each reply must land within 150 ms of that verifier's expected round trip. That pins a key to a region about 1,500 km wide. More than 5 keys sharing one region and one ASN split a single reward. A 300-key farm on a walnut-sized rack can't fake three distances at once, and scattering it like karst caves across 60 cities means renting 60 real servers. Every ping is logged, so peers can audit the thread.
